summary: Adversarial expert panel pressure-tests the Wick+Ruffle+swf-crate integration plan

findings.title: "swf crate v0.2.2" is two different crates: crates.io 0.2.2 is frozen at 2025-01-20 while the in-repo crate kept the same version through 40+ commits
findings.attack: The plan pins "swf crate v0.2.2 (lives inside the Ruffle monorepo)" as if those are one thing. crates.io swf 0.2.2 was published 2025-01-20; the monorepo's swf/Cargo.toml still says 0.2.2 today, but 40 commits have touched swf/ since that publish (edition-2024 migration, PlaceObject/allEventFlags support, multiple reader fixes). `cargo add swf@0.2.2` gets you an 18-month-old API snapshot that will not match code written against master's source (e.g. PointDelta, write_ubits_ct); worse, your writer and the Ruffle player/exporter you differential-test against would come from different eras of the format model.
findings.evidence: index.crates.io/3/s/swf (versions end at 0.2.2), crates.io API /crates/swf/0.2.2 (created_at 2025-01-20, not yanked), raw swf/Cargo.toml on master (version = "0.2.2"), GitHub commits API: 40 commits touching swf/ since 2025-01-21
findings.fix: Depend on the swf crate via a git dependency pinned to a specific ruffle-rs/ruffle rev, and use that SAME rev for the exporter/WASM player used in testing (one submodule or one [patch] rev). Never reference the crates.io release; treat its 0.2.2 number as a decoy.

findings.title: "Wick Path -> DefineShape" without a version choice will silently drop alpha, reject stroke styles, and mis-fill self-intersecting paths
findings.attack: The v1 mapping says just "DefineShape". The Shape struct has a version field 1-4 and the writer behaves very differently per version: write_line_style/write_gradient call write_rgb (alpha silently discarded) for shape_version < 3; any non-Color line fill or cap/join/miter control (LineStyle2, which is what paper.js strokeCap/strokeJoin need) returns Error("Complex line styles can only be used in DefineShape4 tags") for version < 4; and the nonzero winding rule — paper.js's DEFAULT fillRule — is only expressible via ShapeFlag::NON_ZERO_WINDING_RULE, which the writer only emits for version >= 4 (flags byte written only in the `shape.version >= 4` branch of write_define_shape). Wick colors are RGBA and hand-drawn/boolean-united paths self-intersect, so DefineShape1/2 output would render visibly wrong with no compile error.
findings.evidence: swf/src/write.rs write_define_shape (version-gated edge_bounds/flags), write_line_style lines 1583-1615, write_gradient rgb/rgba branch; swf/src/types.rs ShapeFlag::NON_ZERO_WINDING_RULE (line 658). paper.js nonzero default is from knowledge, not fetched.
findings.fix: Make DefineShape4 the unconditional v1 target: always populate edge_bounds, set NON_ZERO_WINDING_RULE when the paper.js fillRule is nonzero (its default), and use LineStyle2 flags for caps/joins. Document in wick2swf that versions 1-3 are not supported output.

findings.title: Phase 0 unknown (a) is already answered: avm1::write IS public — but it's a Writer method, DoAction takes raw bytes, and you must append Action::End yourself
findings.attack: The plan spends Phase 0 effort settling "whether write_action is publicly reachable." It is: lib.rs has `pub mod avm1`, avm1.rs has `pub mod write`, and `pub fn write_action(&mut self, action: &Action)` is a public method on `pub struct Writer<W: Write>` (avm1/write.rs:8,79). The real gotchas are adjacent: (1) Tag::DoAction is `pub type DoAction<'a> = &'a [u8]` — you serialize actions into a Vec first and the Tag borrows it, so all action buffers must outlive tag-list construction (Tag<'a> lifetimes force an arena/owned-buffer pattern across the whole compiler); (2) the action block terminator is not automatic — you must write Action::End (OpCode 0) as the last action or players will read past the block.
findings.evidence: raw swf/src/lib.rs, swf/src/avm1.rs, swf/src/avm1/write.rs lines 8/68/79, swf/src/types.rs line 1793 (pub type DoAction<'a> = &'a [u8])
findings.fix: Delete unknown (a) from Phase 0's charter (keep the hello-square anyway for unknown (b)). In wick2swf, design tag construction around an owned byte-buffer arena from day one, and wrap action emission in a helper that always terminates with Action::End.

findings.title: Header.num_frames and Sprite.num_frames are caller-supplied, never derived — and write_tag_list already appends Tag::End
findings.attack: write_swf_raw_tags writes header.num_frames verbatim and write_define_sprite writes sprite.num_frames verbatim; nothing counts your ShowFrame tags. A wick2swf that computes layers/frames in one pass and frame counts in another will eventually emit a mismatch (Ruffle uses the root count for totalFrames/progress; sprite mismatches confuse gotoAndPlay in Phase 3). Separately, write_tag_list appends an implicit Tag::End (write.rs:2397-2404) — hand-adding Tag::End to the tag Vec double-terminates the stream.
findings.evidence: swf/src/write.rs write_swf_raw_tags (lines 49-66), write_define_sprite (lines 1343-1354), write_tag_list (line 2397, "Implicit end tag")
findings.fix: Compute num_frames as the count of ShowFrame tags in the same function that finalizes each timeline's tag list (root and every sprite), and never push Tag::End manually.

findings.title: Baked-tween mapping omits opacity: Wick tweens interpolate opacity, which is a PlaceObject color_transform, not part of the matrix
findings.attack: The plan bakes "the interpolated transform matrix per frame," but Wick's Tween.interpolate lerps x, y, scaleX, scaleY, rotation, skew AND opacity (Tween.js:87 in the StickmanRed fork), plus fullRotations. Opacity cannot ride the matrix; it must be emitted as PlaceObject.color_transform (alpha multiplier) on the same per-frame Modify tags. Fade tweens — the single most nostalgic Flash idiom — would silently export as fully opaque. (fullRotations is fine as long as you sample Wick's own interpolation then build the matrix, rather than lerping matrices.)
findings.evidence: raw StickmanRed/wick-editor engine/src/base/Tween.js (interpolated props list incl. opacity, fullRotations); swf/src/types.rs PlaceObject.color_transform field
findings.fix: Extend the v1 tween mapping to "matrix + ColorTransform per frame": sample Wick's interpolate(), split into Matrix (x/y/scale/rotation/skew) and ColorTransform (opacity -> alpha_multiply), set both on each baked PlaceObject{version:2, action:Modify}.

findings.title: Golden-PNG CI via the exporter means building the full Ruffle monorepo with wgpu and installing software Vulkan
findings.attack: The exporter is an unpublished binary crate (version.workspace, not on crates.io) depending on ruffle_render_wgpu — so "golden reference PNGs rendered by Ruffle's exporter crate in CI" implies compiling the whole Ruffle player + wgpu stack from source in CI and having a Vulkan device on a GPU-less runner. It is workable — Ruffle's own test_rust.yml installs mesa-vulkan-drivers (lavapipe) and gates render tests behind an imgtests feature — but it's a 20-40 min cold build plus driver setup the plan doesn't budget, and lavapipe output differs subtly from your desktop GPU (goldens must be generated by the same backend that checks them).
findings.evidence: raw exporter/Cargo.toml (bin deps: ruffle_core, ruffle_render_wgpu; no lib target), raw .github/workflows/test_rust.yml (LINUX_DEPENDENCIES: mesa-vulkan-drivers; imgtests feature)
findings.fix: Copy Ruffle's own recipe: pin the monorepo rev (same one as the swf dependency), apt-get mesa-vulkan-drivers, cache the cargo build aggressively, and generate goldens inside CI on lavapipe (never on the dev machine's GPU). Alternatively run goldens locally only and keep CI to the cheaper structural/round-trip (write_swf -> parse_swf) tests.

findings.title: The hard 20% of the shape compiler is fill_style_0/1 edge-side semantics plus quantization noise in the frame-diff oracle
findings.attack: "paper.js fills/strokes mapped to SWF FillStyle/LineStyle" understates the model gap: SWF shapes are an edge soup where each StyleChange selects a LEFT fill (fill_style_0) and RIGHT fill (fill_style_1) per edge run — not per-path fill attributes. With NON_ZERO_WINDING_RULE set (per the DefineShape4 finding), subpath direction now matters, so compound paths with holes must have consistent winding and correct side assignment or holes fill in. Separately, twips quantization (1/20 px) plus cubic->quadratic subdivision guarantees the differential oracle's per-pixel diffs concentrate on edges; a naive tolerance either drowns in edge noise or masks real bugs.
findings.evidence: swf/src/types.rs StyleChangeData {fill_style_0, fill_style_1, line_style, new_styles} (lines 747-753), ShapeRecord edge variants; diff-noise argument is reasoning only
findings.fix: In phase 1, write the fill-side assignment as its own documented module (paper.js path direction -> consistent winding -> fill_style_1 on outer, matching holes), with hole-in-square and figure-eight fixtures first. For the oracle, compare with an edge-dilated mask (ignore a 1-2px band around detected edges) or a perceptual metric, and keep exact-match assertions to the parsed-SWF structural level (write_swf then parse_swf round-trip).

result.verdict_reason: The v1 tag mappings are fundamentally correct against the real crate: Tag::PlaceObject carries a version field plus PlaceObjectAction::Modify, so baked tweens as per-frame move-at-depth work exactly as planned; DefineSprite nests Tag lists recursively; the writer computes style-bit counts and edge sbits itself; avm1::write::Writer::write_action is public, resolving Phase 0's unknown (a) in the plan's favor. But two things need changing before Phase 1: pin the swf crate as a git dependency (crates.io 0.2.2 is an 18-month-old snapshot wearing the same version number as master), and commit to DefineShape4 as the only output shape version (alpha, caps/joins, and paper.js's nonzero fill rule all require it, and lower versions fail silently or hard).

swf/src/avm1.rs + avm1/write.rs — pub mod write; pub fn write_action as method on pub Writer (line 79)
swf/src/avm1/types.rs — Action enum with End variant; write_action dispatch covers full opcode set
crates.io index (index.crates.io/3/s/swf) — published versions 0.1.0..0.2.2; crates.io API — 0.2.2 published 2025-01-20, not yanked

swf/src/types.rs (full file) — Tag enum, PlaceObject{version, action, matrix, color_transform, ratio...}, PlaceObjectAction::{Place,Modify,Replace}, Shape{version, flags}, ShapeFlag::NON_ZERO_WINDING_RULE, ShapeRecord, StyleChangeData fill_style_0/1, FillStyle, LineStyle/LineStyleFlag, DoAction = &[u8], RemoveObject{character_id: Option} (RemoveObject2 selection)

what_i_could_not_check: Ruffle's loader-side leniency on header/tag ordering (FileAttributes absence, SetBackgroundColor position) — would require reading ruffle_core's loader or running a player; Phase 0's hello-square is the right way to settle this and should stay

Exact API diffs between crates.io swf 0.2.2 and master (I verified 40 commits of divergence exist, not the specific breaking changes)
Whether crates.io API results are affected by the earlier data-access block (the versioned endpoint responded fine with a UA header)
Actual lavapipe-vs-GPU rendering deltas for the golden-PNG pipeline — reasoning from Ruffle's CI setup only

findings.title: "Building on modern Node" is the wrong goal — this stack builds ONLY on Node 14, and that's fine
findings.attack: Phase 2 says "get the StickmanRed fork building on modern Node." The dependency set makes that a multi-week CRA migration, not a build fix. Verified pins: react-scripts 2.0.5 (webpack 4.19.1 in package-lock.json — MD4 hashing crashes on Node >=17 under OpenSSL 3), node-sass 4.14.1 (prebuilt bindings stop at Node 14 / ABI 83; source builds need libsass + python2-era node-gyp, dead on modern toolchains), lockfileVersion 1 (npm 6). 'Modern Node' means upgrading react-scripts 2->5 across a 40-dependency 2018-era app (react 16, reactstrap 6, react-dnd 11...), which is exactly the weeks-long rot-fixing the plan hopes to avoid. Meanwhile the fork's maintainer demonstrably builds it today: the gh-pages branch was deployed 2026-07-09, two weeks ago — proof the build works in SOME environment, and that environment is old Node, not modern Node.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com StickmanRed/wick-editor master package.json + package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 1, node-sass 4.14.1, webpack 4.19.1, react-scripts 2.0.5); api.github.com branches + gh-pages commit log (deploy 2026-07-09); HTTP 200 HEAD on github.com/sass/node-sass/releases/download/v4.14.1/linux-x64-83_binding.node (prebuilt Node-14 binary still downloadable)
findings.fix: Rewrite the Phase 2 goal as: pin Node 14 via nvm (`nvm install 14` — bundles npm 6, matching the v1 lockfile) and build as-is. node-sass 4.14.1's linux-x64-83 prebuilt binding is still served (verified 200), so no native compile is needed. Do NOT attempt react-scripts upgrade; the fork's own 'updgrading-react' branch (react-scripts 4, react 17) died in Feb 2021 — treat that as the cautionary tale. With the pin, Phase 2 is 2–5 days; without it, weeks.

findings.title: The engine build can be skipped entirely — the editor consumes a committed prebuilt bundle that the fork keeps current
findings.attack: The plan treats 'get the fork building' as one lump including the engine. It isn't: the editor loads a prebuilt engine bundle committed at public/corelibs/wick-engine/wickengine.js (2.27 MB), and the gulp engine build (`build-engine` script) only regenerates that file. Critically, the fork's maintainer keeps it current — the committed wickengine.js was last updated 2026-06-27 in the same 'Add different tween methods and inspector clip skew' commit that is the fork's HEAD. So Phase 2 (Export button, Ruffle tab — pure React/UI work) never needs gulp, babel-for-engine, or the engine toolchain at all. Only if wick2swf later needs engine-side changes does that build matter, and even then it's a self-contained gulp-concat pipeline, far simpler than the CRA build.
findings.evidence: api.github.com contents listing of public/corelibs/wick-engine (wickengine.js 2268756 bytes); commits?path=public/corelibs/wick-engine/wickengine.js shows 2026-06-27 update; package.json build-engine script; engine/package.json (gulp-only devDeps)
findings.fix: State in the plan: consume the committed wickengine.js as-is; engine build is out of Phase 2 scope. This also gives a zero-build fallback for early experimentation — the gh-pages branch holds a complete deployed editor build (2026-07-09) you can serve locally while wick2swf Phase 1 proceeds.

findings.title: The +54 fork commits gave you zero build-config help — and there is no CI anywhere
findings.attack: Any hope that the active fork modernized the build is false. Diffing package.json between Wicklets/master and StickmanRed/master: the ONLY dependency change in 5.5 years of fork activity is underscore ^1.9.1 -> ^1.13.7, plus gh-pages deploy-script tweaks and the homepage URL. react-scripts, node-sass, electron 7, react 16 are all untouched 2020 pins. The fork also has no CI (.github contains only FUNDING.yml, ISSUE_TEMPLATE, images — no workflows dir), so 'it builds for the maintainer' rests entirely on the gh-pages deploy timestamps, on an undocumented local environment. If the maintainer's machine setup is exotic, you find out the hard way.
findings.evidence: diff of Wicklets vs StickmanRed package.json (fetched both); api.github.com contents of .github (no workflows); branch list
findings.fix: Budget for reconstructing the build environment yourself (Node 14 + npm 6 per finding 1) rather than copying a documented one. First deliverable of Phase 2 should be a .nvmrc + a 10-line BUILD.md in your fork so the environment is pinned before any code changes — and it doubles as the thing you'd need anyway if the StickmanRed fork ever goes dark.

findings.title: "Compiler via WASM build" collides with webpack 4 / CRA2 — route WASM around the bundler, not through it
findings.attack: Phase 2 offers 'compiler via WASM build or a local helper process' as equal options. They aren't. Importing a wasm-bindgen module through react-scripts 2.0.5's webpack 4.19.1 pipeline means either ejecting (permanent 2018-config maintenance) or ancient react-app-rewired hacks; CRA2 predates workable wasm/asyncWebAssembly support and craco doesn't target CRA2. Anyone who tries `import init from 'wick2swf'` inside this app loses days to loader errors. The same trap applies to the Ruffle preview tab if Ruffle is installed as an npm dependency and bundled.
findings.evidence: package-lock.json webpack 4.19.1 / react-scripts 2.0.5 (fetched); WASM-loader limitations of webpack 4-era CRA argued from knowledge, not tested this session
findings.fix: Make the plan explicit: (a) preferred — the Phase 1 CLI already exists, so 'Export SWF' shells out to a local helper process (matches the electron.js main-process path the app already has, or a tiny localhost daemon for the browser build); (b) if WASM, build with `wasm-bindgen --target web`, drop the .wasm/.js pair into public/, and load at runtime via fetch/dynamic script — completely bypassing webpack. Embed Ruffle the same way: self-hosted ruffle.js in public/ via script tag (Ruffle's own documented pattern), never through the CRA bundle.

findings.title: postinstall 'electron-builder install-app-deps' will trip npm install for a browser-only workflow
findings.attack: package.json has "postinstall": "electron-builder install-app-deps" — every `npm install` invokes electron-builder 22 with electron 7 devDependencies. For Phase 2's browser-editor goal this is pure dead weight and the most likely single point of install failure (electron-builder 22 native-deps probing on a 2026 OS). The electron 7.3.3 binary itself is still downloadable (verified 200), so it may limp through, but it downloads ~70 MB of Electron you don't need and adds electron-osx-sign/notarize-era scripts to the failure surface.
findings.evidence: package.json scripts + devDependencies (fetched); HTTP 200 on electron-v7.3.3-linux-x64.zip release asset
findings.fix: In your fork's first commit: delete the postinstall script and the electron* devDependencies (or install with --ignore-scripts as an interim). The desktop packaging path is a non-goal for this project — Ruffle desktop covers local playback.

result.verdict_reason: Phase 2 is genuinely days-not-weeks, but only on the opposite of the plan's stated approach: the fork builds today (gh-pages deployed 2026-07-09) on OLD Node, and 'building on modern Node' is a weeks-long CRA migration trap. Pin Node 14 (node-sass 4.14.1 prebuilt binding verified still downloadable), consume the committed 2.27 MB wickengine.js (kept current through the fork's 2026-06-27 HEAD commit — engine build fully skippable), strip the electron postinstall, and keep WASM/Ruffle out of the webpack 4 bundle. With those four changes the phase is low-risk.

Branch list: gh-pages exists, last deploy commit 2026-07-09 (maintainer builds successfully two weeks ago); 'updgrading-react' branch (react-scripts 4) dead since 2021-02

engine/package.json: gulp-only toolchain, separate from CRA build
Release-asset liveness: node-sass v4.14.1 linux-x64-83_binding.node HTTP 200; electron v7.3.3 linux-x64 zip HTTP 200
what_i_could_not_check: Did not actually run npm install / npm run build on Node 14 (read-only session, no clone) — the days-not-weeks estimate rests on lockfile+binding evidence plus the maintainer's 2026-07-09 deploy, not a local repro
The maintainer's actual build environment (no CI, no .nvmrc, no docs) — Node 14 is inferred from the dependency set, not documented
webpack 4 WASM-loading pain argued from knowledge of CRA2 era, not reproduced this session
Whether react-scripts 2.0.5's dev server has any 2026-specific breakage (e.g. against current browsers) beyond the build itself

findings.title: Cross-renderer pixel diff (Wick canvas vs Ruffle) is the wrong CI oracle for its main target
findings.attack: The plan's primary test oracle — frame-diff Wick's paper.js canvas render against Ruffle's wgpu render 'within a tolerance' — cannot cleanly gate the thing it exists to test. The two renderers differ structurally: canvas 2D analytic antialiasing vs wgpu MSAA, different default stroke caps/joins (paper.js butt/miter vs Flash centered round), Flash hairline minimum-width stroke behavior, plus deliberate geometry perturbation from the plan's own cubic-to-quadratic subdivision. Ruffle's OWN test framework needs per-test tolerance + max_outliers even comparing Ruffle-to-Ruffle across backends (tests/framework/src/options/image_comparison.rs) — two unrelated renderers are strictly worse. The killer: the tolerance loose enough to pass AA/stroke noise will swallow exactly the bugs the harness targets — tween-baking easing errors, which appear as subpixel-to-few-pixel position offsets on mid-tween frames. And the StickmanRed fork just added 'different tween methods' (verified tip commit), so wick2swf must reimplement the fork's easing math in Rust — the highest-risk code, and the diff is blind to it at workable tolerances. Also fork fixtures will contain gradient fills (fork has a gradient tool) while v1 says 'gradients maybe', guaranteeing large legitimate diffs. Finally, running Wick's engine headless requires puppeteer/headless Chrome in CI (it's a browser CRA app), the heaviest possible harness dependency.
findings.evidence: Fetched: ruffle-rs/ruffle tests/framework/src/options/image_comparison.rs (tolerance/max_outliers/checks machinery); exporter/src/exporter.rs (wgpu-only pipeline); gh api StickmanRed/wick-editor commits ('Add different tween methods and inspector clip skew', 'Gradient tool (#46)', 'Layer opacity'). AA/stroke-semantics argument is reasoning from renderer knowledge.
findings.fix: Replace the differential pixel gate with a 3-layer oracle: (1) STRUCTURAL, the real workhorse — parse the emitted SWF back with swf::parse_swf and assert on tags, depths, and per-frame PlaceObject matrices; generate expected tween matrices with a small Node script that calls the FORK'S OWN easing code and dumps JSON, so the Rust easing reimplementation is tested numerically with zero pixels involved; (2) Ruffle-only golden frames via the exporter with tolerance+max_outliers (finding 2); (3) demote Wick-canvas-vs-Ruffle to a manual side-by-side eyeball tool in the editor preview tab, never a CI gate.

findings.title: Golden-frame CI is real, but goldens must be blessed on the CI backend (lavapipe), not a local GPU
findings.attack: The 'golden reference PNGs rendered by Ruffle's exporter crate in CI' step works — but only if generation and comparison use the same wgpu backend. The exporter has no CPU rasterizer of its own (exporter.rs: create_wgpu_instance/request_adapter_and_device, wgpu-only; --graphics flag selects backend); headless CI works because Mesa's lavapipe provides software Vulkan — Ruffle's own test_rust.yml installs mesa-vulkan-drivers on plain ubuntu-24.04 GitHub runners and enables imgtests there, proving the path. If the author renders goldens on their local GPU and CI compares on lavapipe, edge AA differs on every shape boundary: either exact-match goldens flake from day 1 or tolerance gets inflated until useless. Two smaller costs hiding in the same step: the exporter is not a published crate/binary, so CI must build it from the ruffle monorepo (a full ruffle_core+wgpu compile, easily 15-30 min uncached), and exporter frame semantics need pinning down once (frame N = --skipframes N-1 --frames 1; run_frame-then-capture; ruffle_core's 'deterministic' feature is already enabled in exporter's Cargo.toml).
findings.evidence: Fetched: exporter/src/exporter.rs, exporter/src/cli.rs, exporter/Cargo.toml (features = ['deterministic', 'default_font']), and .github/workflows/test_rust.yml (LINUX_DEPENDENCIES: mesa-vulkan-drivers; 'Enable image tests' on non-macOS runners).
findings.fix: Bless goldens in CI itself (a manual 'regenerate goldens' workflow that commits lavapipe-rendered PNGs), or force lavapipe locally when blessing (VK_ICD_FILENAMES pointed at the lvp ICD, exporter --graphics vulkan). Copy Ruffle's comparison shape: per-fixture tolerance + max_outliers rather than exact match. Cache the built exporter binary keyed on the pinned ruffle git rev.

findings.title: 'swf crate v0.2.2' is two different codebases; pin writer and player to one ruffle git rev
findings.attack: The plan names 'the ruffle-rs swf crate v0.2.2'. crates.io's swf 0.2.2 was last published 2025-01-20; the monorepo's swf/Cargo.toml still declares version 0.2.2 today with ~18 months of unpublished changes on master. If wick2swf depends on crates.io while the preview WASM / exporter / desktop player are nightly builds from master, the writer and the oracle disagree on the format surface (and the appendix's verified type signatures were read from master, not from the published crate — they may not match crates.io 0.2.2).
findings.evidence: Fetched: crates.io/api/v1/crates/swf (max_version 0.2.2, updated_at 2025-01-20) and raw swf/Cargo.toml on master (version = "0.2.2").
findings.fix: Depend on swf as a git dependency pinned to a specific ruffle-rs/ruffle revision, and build the CI exporter and the embedded preview WASM from that same revision. Bump all three together deliberately.

findings.title: Phase 2: route Ruffle around webpack 4, not through it; use the byte-loading API for preview
findings.attack: Importing @ruffle-rs/ruffle as an npm module through the CRA fork's webpack-4 pipeline is the landmine: webpack 4's half-native wasm handling plus wasm-bindgen's loader conventions plus CRA's no-eject config means fighting the bundler for days. The plan doesn't commit to a mechanism, so the risk is drifting into the npm-import path by default. Same trap doubled if wick2swf itself is compiled to WASM and imported through webpack 4 (the plan's 'compiler via WASM build' option).
findings.evidence: Fetched: web/packages/core/README.md (documents the script-tag/selfhosted API, window.RufflePlayer.newest().createPlayer(), and warns the .wasm file must be served with the correct MIME type) and web/packages/core/src/public/config/load-options.ts (DataLoadOptions.data: ArrayLike<number> | ArrayBuffer at line ~833, so the preview tab can load freshly-exported SWF bytes with no server round-trip). Setup docs show no COOP/COEP requirement — cross-origin isolation is a non-issue. Webpack-4-specific breakage is argued from knowledge, not reproduced.
findings.fix: Drop the ruffle-selfhosted release files into the CRA public/ directory and load via script tag (bypasses webpack entirely); feed the preview tab with player.ruffle().load({ data: exportedBytes }). Check the dev server serves .wasm as application/wasm. For the compiler, prefer the local-helper-process option over a wick2swf WASM build while the editor is still on webpack 4.

findings.title: Tier-0 AVM1 is fine — and Phase 0 unknown (a) is already settled; one trap: use PRESS, not MOUSE_DOWN
findings.attack: Mostly an all-clear with two corrections. (1) The plan lists 'whether swf's avm1::write is publicly reachable' as a Phase-0 open unknown — it isn't open: swf/src/lib.rs declares `pub mod avm1;`, so write_action is reachable from outside the crate. (2) Tier-0 'on-click handlers' looks like it collides with 'buttons OUT of v1', but doesn't need DefineButton2: PlaceObject ClipActions with ClipEventFlag::PRESS/RELEASE gives per-clip button-like click handling (hit area = the clip's shapes, hand cursor). The trap is grabbing MOUSE_DOWN instead — that fires stage-globally on any click, not on the clip — and forgetting PRESS is SWF6+, so the header must declare version >= 6. stop/play/gotoAndPlay are plain DoAction tags; no gaps.
findings.evidence: Fetched: swf/src/lib.rs (pub mod avm1) and swf/src/types.rs (ClipEventFlag bitflags: MOUSE_DOWN = 1<<4 vs PRESS = 1<<10 / RELEASE = 1<<11, comment 'Added in SWF6'; ClipAction { events, key_code, action_data }).
findings.fix: Strike unknown (a) from Phase 0 (keep (b), the Ruffle header/tag-ordering check — that one still needs the hello-square). For Tier-0 clicks: emit PlaceObject clip actions with ClipEventFlag::PRESS | RELEASE on the target sprite, and set the SWF header version to 6+ (just use a high version like 8 throughout).

result.verdict_reason: Ruffle works in both roles the plan assigns it — the exporter renders frame N to PNG headlessly (proven by Ruffle's own CI on stock GitHub runners with lavapipe), and the preview tab has a clean script-tag + load-from-ArrayBuffer path that sidesteps webpack 4 entirely. The one design that should not survive review is the cross-renderer differential pixel gate: even Ruffle-vs-Ruffle comparison needs tolerance machinery, and the tolerance that absorbs antialiasing/stroke noise is blind to the easing-math errors the harness most needs to catch (made sharper by the fork's newly added tween methods). Swap it for structural SWF round-trip assertions plus Ruffle-only lavapipe-blessed golden frames, and the rest of the oracle/preview architecture holds.

findings.title: DefineShape has no fill rule — brush/potrace CompoundPaths and self-intersecting paths need a planarization pass the plan omits
findings.attack: The v1 mapping 'Wick Path (paper.js path JSON, cubic beziers) -> DefineShape' treats shape compilation as subdivision + unit conversion + style mapping. It is not. Wick's brush tool output is potrace-vectorized geometry: Brush.js:356-368 runs potrace.fromImage(...).toSVG, imports it, and takes children[0] — for any stroke with a loop or enclosed hole this is a paper.js CompoundPath with multiple subpaths where holes are expressed by winding. paper.js fills with the nonzero rule; SWF DefineShape has no fill rule at all — fill is determined per-edge by FillStyle0/FillStyle1 (which fill is on each side of each edge). A naive converter that emits every subpath with the same fill-on-one-side gives filled-in holes (an 'O' brush stroke renders as a disc). Worse, a single self-intersecting closed path (easy to draw with the pencil) fills all lobes under nonzero but behaves even-odd-like under SWF's edge-side model — lobes silently drop out. This is the classic hard part of every real SWF exporter and it is absent from the plan.
findings.evidence: Fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com (StickmanRed/wick-editor master): engine/src/tools/Brush.js (potrace pipeline, lines 320-368), engine/src/view/paper-ext/Path.potrace.js (children[0] extraction), engine/src/base/Path.js (json = raw paper exportJSON, line 39). SWF fill-side model from spec knowledge.
findings.fix: Add an explicit geometry-normalization stage to Phase 1: (a) resolve self-intersections (boolean self-union under nonzero rule, i.e. planarize), (b) re-wind so holes are opposite-wound and non-crossing, (c) assign FillStyle0/1 per edge from winding. Add brush-drawn donut and self-crossing pencil-fill fixtures to the differential harness — these are exactly the 'renders but wrong' cases the oracle must catch.

findings.title: 'Sample the interpolated transform matrix' hides two incompatible tween semantics — the fork's default routes through paper.Matrix.decompose and a buggy reconstruct
findings.attack: The plan's tween-baking step assumes one obvious interpolation. The StickmanRed fork (the exact commit the plan cites, 'Add different tween methods') introduced tweenMethod with default 'normal': Tween.interpolate converts both endpoint transforms to paper-decomposed values (Transformation.paperValues -> paper.Matrix.decompose()), lerps those, then reconstructs via Transformation.toMatrixPaper, then re-decomposes via fromMatrix. toMatrixPaper (engine/src/Transformation.js:132-151) contains a dead guard — `if (skew.x === 0)` where skew is a number, so `undefined === 0` is always false — and computes `c = (at - b*d) / a` where a = cos(rotation)·scaleX, which is NaN/blow-up when the lerped rotation crosses ±90°, plus `b = sqrt(r²-a²)·sign(rotate)` which breaks under negative scale (flips). Upstream Wicklets interpolated x/y/scaleX/scaleY/rotation/opacity directly with no skew channel. The compiler must pick: bug-for-bug replication of the fork chain (requires porting paper.Matrix.decompose semantics to Rust) or the sane direct lerp — and whichever it picks, the differential oracle will report divergence on rotation/skew/flip tweens that are NOT compiler bugs. fullRotations (valB += fullRotations*360, Tween.js:100) and the 27 Tween.js easing functions must also be replicated exactly.
findings.evidence: Fetched Tween.js and Transformation.js from StickmanRed/wick-editor master and diffed Tween.js against Wicklets/wick-editor master — the decompose-based 'normal' path is fork-only; upstream is plain per-property lerp.
findings.fix: Decide the sampling semantics as a written spec item in Phase 1 before the harness exists: implement Rust replicas of Tween.interpolate for BOTH tweenMethods (including paper.Matrix.decompose and toMatrixPaper, dead branch and all) so baked frames match editor preview, OR patch the fork to the sane semantics first and compile that. Add rotation-through-90°, flip (negative scale), and skew-tween fixtures; without them the NaN edge ships silently.

findings.title: Opacity is a first-class tweened channel but the plan bakes only the matrix — fades silently don't fade
findings.attack: Wick.Transformation carries opacity (0-1), Tween.interpolate lerps it, and View.Clip.render applies it as group.opacity. The plan's baked-tween mapping is 'sample the interpolated transform matrix per frame and emit one PlaceObject per frame' — a matrix cannot express opacity. Without emitting a ColorTransform (CXFORM alpha multiplier) on each PlaceObject, every fade tween exports as a hard fully-opaque object: renders, plays, wrong. Path-level opacity (Path.js opacity getter/setter) additionally requires baking alpha into RGBA fills, i.e. DefineShape3 minimum, which the plan never pins down. Second-order trap for the oracle: paper.js group opacity composites the group offscreen then blends (overlaps inside a 50%-opaque clip show single density), while SWF cxform alpha multiplies per shape (overlaps show double density) — a guaranteed frame-diff mismatch on any translucent clip with overlapping children.
findings.evidence: Fetched Transformation.js (opacity field), Tween.js (opacity in the lerped property list, line 87), View.Clip.js (group.opacity = transformation.opacity, line 177), and ruffle-rs/ruffle swf/src/types.rs (PlaceObject.color_transform: Option<ColorTransform> at line 319 — the crate supports the fix).
findings.fix: Extend the baked-tween emitter: per sampled frame emit matrix + CXFORM alpha (PlaceObject.color_transform). Pin DefineShape3 as the v1 shape tag so path opacity bakes into RGBA fill/line colors. Document the group-vs-per-shape opacity compositing divergence and either exclude overlapping-translucent fixtures from strict diffing or wrap translucent multi-child clips knowingly.

findings.title: Tween application target is underspecified: the tween overwrites the transformation of EVERY clip on the frame and never touches loose paths
findings.attack: The plan maps 'Wick Tween -> baked PlaceObject per frame' without saying what the tween transforms. The actual semantics (Frame.js applyTweenTransforms, line 564): the active tween's transformation is copied ABSOLUTELY onto every clip on the frame (clip.transformation = tween.transformation.copy() — replacement, not composition), and loose Wick.Paths on the same frame are not transformed at all. Frame.createTween (Frame.js:465-493) auto-wraps content into one clip whose origin is the selection-bounds center only at creation time — but nothing prevents a user from later adding a loose path or a second clip to a tweened frame. A compiler that models the tween as 'transform the frame's content' (e.g. wrapping the frame in one sprite and tweening it) renders wrong for path+clip or multi-clip frames. Pivot chain, for the record: clip children are re-based by addObjects (Clip.js:436-440, object.x -= transformation.x), and View.Clip.render pivots the group at (0,0) before setting the matrix — so PlaceObject.matrix = clip.transformation.toMatrix() maps directly IF DefineSprite geometry is emitted in clip-local coordinates; Transformation.toMatrix's [a,b,c,d,tx,ty] maps 1:1 onto SWF MATRIX [ScaleX, RotateSkew0, RotateSkew1, ScaleY, TranslateX, TranslateY] in the same y-down convention.
findings.evidence: Fetched Frame.js (applyTweenTransforms, createTween), Clip.js (addObjects re-basing), View.Clip.js (pivot=(0,0), matrix.set(toMatrix())), Transformation.js (toMatrix) from StickmanRed/wick-editor master.
findings.fix: Spec the mapping precisely in Phase 1: per sampled frame, apply the tween transform to each clip's PlaceObject individually (identical matrix for all clips, replacement semantics); loose paths keep static placement. Add two fixtures: (tweened frame with clip + loose path) and (tweened frame with two clips).

findings.title: Layer stacking is reversed relative to SWF depth, and hidden layers render when published
findings.attack: View.Timeline.js:32-34 renders layers filtered by `layer.project.isPublished || !layer.hidden` and then .reverse()d — so Wick layer index 0 (top of the panel) draws LAST and sits frontmost, and hidden layers ARE visible in published/playing output. SWF depth is the opposite convention (higher depth = frontmost). A compiler that maps layer index to depth 1:1 flips the entire z-order of every multi-layer animation, and one that skips hidden layers diverges from Wick's own publish semantics. Within a frame, z-order is the drawable array order with dynamic-text force-fronted (View.Frame.js:88-91).
findings.evidence: Fetched View.Timeline.js and View.Frame.js from StickmanRed/wick-editor master.
findings.fix: depth = (layerCount - layerIndex) band + within-frame drawable index; include hidden layers in export (matching isPublished behavior) or make it an explicit export flag. One multi-layer overlap fixture in the differential harness pins this permanently.

findings.title: Path.json is raw paper.js exportJSON — the compiler must handle relative handles, shorthand segments, multiple item classes, and non-string colors
findings.attack: Path.js:39 stores `path.exportJSON({asString:false})` verbatim; the .wick format therefore contains paper.js serialization quirks the plan's 'cubic beziers -> DefineShape' line glosses over: (a) segment JSON is [[x,y],[inX,inY],[outX,outY]] where handleIn/handleOut are RELATIVE to the anchor — treating them as absolute produces garbage curves that still 'render'; (b) segments without handles serialize as bare [x,y]; (c) the top-level class can be 'Path', 'CompoundPath', 'Raster' (image paths exist in the base model — Path.js createImagePath — and are not on the plan's exclusion list even though bitmaps need DefineBits* tags), 'PointText', or 'Group' (SVG asset imports); (d) fillColor/strokeColor serialize as hex strings OR normalized float arrays. Separately, emitting SWF edge deltas by rounding per-delta accumulates twip drift along long potrace outlines — round absolute coordinates and emit deltas of the rounded values, or adjacent fills develop hairline seams.
findings.evidence: Fetched Path.js (exportJSON storage, createImagePath/Raster branch, 'asset:uuid' source rewriting in _serialize). Segment/color serialization formats from paper.js knowledge (not re-fetched this session).
findings.fix: Phase 1 spec: enumerate accepted item classes with an explicit reject-or-degrade rule for Raster/PointText/Group (add 'images' to the OUT-of-v1 list — right now it is not there); write a paper-JSON decoder test corpus straight from fixture .wick files before writing any geometry code; implement round-then-delta twip emission.

result.verdict_reason: The architecture (fork editor, standalone Rust compiler, Ruffle oracle) holds, and I confirmed a plan-favorable fact along the way: swf's avm1 module is `pub mod avm1` / `pub mod write`, so Phase 0's open unknown (a) is already resolved positively. But the v1 mappings understate the two genuinely hard semantic gaps: SWF's fill-rule-less, per-edge fill model versus paper.js nonzero winding (brush output is potrace CompoundPaths — a planarization/winding-normalization pass is mandatory, not implied by 'cubics to quadratics'), and the fork's brand-new decompose-based default tween interpolation (with a dead branch and a divide-by-cos(rotation)), which makes 'sample the interpolated matrix' an underspecified statement the differential oracle will punish. Opacity baking (CXFORM) and per-clip tween application are concrete spec gaps that would ship silent wrong renders. All fixable within Phase 1 if specified now.

Wicklets/wick-editor master engine/src/base/Tween.js — diffed against the fork to isolate the new tweenMethod='normal' decompose-based interpolation as fork-only

Actual structural output of the oov potrace JS library's toSVG (subpath winding direction of holes) — inferred from potrace conventions; worth dumping one real brush stroke's JSON from a running editor early in Phase 1

Whether Wick's eraser/boolean pipeline can itself produce self-intersecting single paths, or only clean planar output — Brush.js line 419 area suggests boolean cleanup on overlap, but I did not trace the eraser path

findings.title: Phase 2's 'modern Node' goal attacks the exact tarpit that killed upstream; the fork itself never attempted it
findings.attack: Phase 2 says 'get the StickmanRed fork building on modern Node (create-react-app-era dependency rot is a known risk)'. I fetched both package.json files: the fork ships the IDENTICAL 2018 build stack as dead upstream — react-scripts 2.0.5 (webpack 4, breaks on Node 17+ OpenSSL 3) and node-sass ^4.9.4 (no prebuilt binaries past Node 14, native gyp build against ancient APIs). The fork's own README says: 'You'll need NodeJS 14 (NOTE: This is a ancient version of NodeJS, from the ancient times)'. The one active maintainer of this codebase, 54 commits deep, chose NOT to modernize — that is the strongest available evidence about the cost. A react-scripts 2→5 + node-sass→dart-sass migration of a 160MB CRA app is itself a multi-week project with zero nostalgic payoff, and it is precisely the phase where dead-webapp revivals die (upstream Wicklets/wick-editor is the corpse in the room: it stopped in Jan 2021 sitting on this same stack).
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/StickmanRed/wick-editor/master/package.json and .../Wicklets/wick-editor/master/package.json (react-scripts 2.0.5, node-sass ^4.9.4 in both); StickmanRed README.md Node 14 requirement; api.github.com repo sizes (fork 162003 KB)
findings.fix: Delete 'modern Node' as a goal. If/when the fork is needed, build it exactly the way its maintainer does: nvm install 14, done in an afternoon. Never migrate the build stack — this is a personal tool and Node 14 in an nvm sandbox is free.

findings.title: The deployed Wick editor is live today and already produces .wick files — the fork is not on the critical path to the payoff
findings.attack: The plan sequences editor-fork work (Phase 2) as the route to 'draw shapes, press export'. But https://wickeditor.com/editor/ serves the full built editor right now (I fetched it: CRA bundle, wickengine.js, loads fine; note editor.wickeditor.com is broken — curl returns 000, stale alias to wicklets.github.io with no Pages behind it, and the fork has no gh-pages deployment either, 404). Since wick2swf consumes .wick files and the plan keeps the .wick format unchanged, the author can draw in the deployed editor, save .wick, compile, and watch it in Ruffle with ZERO editor work. Option (c) is not one of three equal options — it is strictly dominant for v1, and the plan never says where Phase 1's .wick fixtures come from, which implies the author may believe the fork build gates fixture authoring.
findings.evidence: curl https://wickeditor.com/editor/ (200, full editor HTML with wickengine.js); curl https://editor.wickeditor.com/ (000); api.github.com/repos/StickmanRed/wick-editor/pages (404)
findings.fix: Rewrite Phase 1 to state: all fixtures authored in the live deployed editor at wickeditor.com/editor/ and saved as .wick. Demote Phase 2 to 'Phase 4, optional, only if the deployed editor disappears or the fork's new tween types are wanted' — the only real reasons to build the fork are its post-2021 tween methods and an offline hedge (git clone of the fork + Node 14 covers the hedge without any wiring work).

findings.title: The Wick-JS-vs-Ruffle differential frame-diff oracle is product-grade infrastructure that will eat weeks before any payoff
findings.attack: Phase 1 bundles 'the differential test harness' into the core deliverable. Frame-diffing two unrelated renderers (paper.js canvas vs Ruffle) within a tolerance is a notorious solo-killer: the cubic→quadratic subdivision guarantees geometric divergence by construction, and antialiasing, stroke-join/cap models, and rasterization differences mean every 'failure' is a tolerance-tuning session, not a compiler bug. Worse, running Wick's JS engine headlessly means puppeteer or node-canvas infra — a whole second build system for the test suite of a hobby compiler. This is the classic pattern where the test oracle becomes the project. The plan already contains the right-sized oracle in the same sentence: Ruffle's exporter crate producing golden PNGs.
findings.evidence: reasoning only (renderer-divergence mechanics + the plan's own cubic→quadratic subdivision step)
findings.fix: Cut the Wick-vs-Ruffle differential harness from Phase 1 entirely. v1 oracle = Ruffle exporter golden PNGs (regression pinning) + eyeballing in Ruffle desktop (intent checking). If cross-renderer diffing ever feels needed, it's a Phase-4 luxury after the tool already works.

findings.title: Phase 1 is a monolith that defers the first 'I drew a thing and Ruffle played it' moment behind clips, tweens, and the harness
findings.attack: Phase 0 delivers a hardcoded square in days — good — but that is a programmer payoff, not the nostalgic one. The nostalgic moment is 'I drew something with a pen tool and it plays in Ruffle', and as written it sits behind all of Phase 1: shapes + timeline + clips + baked tweens + differential harness as one unit. Projects like this die mid-Phase-1 with the payoff still ahead of them. A shapes-only compiler (Path→DefineShape, one frame, no tweens, no clips) reading a real .wick saved from the deployed editor is a small increment past hello-square and IS the payoff.
findings.evidence: reasoning only (plan text: Phase 1 scope as written)
findings.fix: Slice Phase 1 into gated milestones: 1a static drawing→single-frame SWF from a real saved .wick (this is the payoff moment — target it within the first couple weeks); 1b frame-by-frame timeline; 1c baked tweens; 1d nested clips. Each milestone ends with 'played it in Ruffle'. The project can now die after 1a and still have been worth it.

findings.title: Phase 3 'on-click handlers' silently reintroduces the button tag family that v1 explicitly excluded
findings.attack: The V1 mappings list buttons as OUT, and Phase 3 promises only a 'FIXED action vocabulary... emitted through the AVM1 assembler'. But on-click in SWF is not just DoAction — it requires DefineButton2 + ButtonCondAction records (or PlaceObject2 clip-event handlers), a new tag family with its own hit-state shape semantics. Phase 3 is therefore bigger than the framing implies, and it's exactly the kind of post-payoff scope that gets started and abandoned half-wired.
findings.evidence: reasoning only (SWF spec structure; plan's own tag-mapping table omits DefineButton2)
findings.fix: Split Phase 3: 3a = frame actions only (stop/play/gotoAndPlay via DoAction — genuinely just the AVM1 assembler, and covers the classic 'looping animation with a stop()' nostalgia case); 3b = buttons/on-click as a separately-decided item with DefineButton2 named in its scope. Author will likely never miss 3b.

findings.title: 'Gradients maybe' and 'compiler via WASM build' are undecided scope leaks in a plan that is otherwise well-fenced
findings.attack: 'Gradients maybe' in a v1 list means gradients get half-implemented during a motivated weekend and then generate FillStyle edge-case bugs forever. And Phase 2's 'WASM build or a local helper process' keeps a wasm-pack + JS-interop workstream alive for what a solo user can do with a file-watcher shell loop (save .wick → wick2swf runs → Ruffle preview reloads).
findings.evidence: reasoning only (plan text)
findings.fix: Decide gradients OUT of v1 now (solid fills + strokes cover the stick-figure nostalgia register). Strike the WASM option; the integration story is 'wick2swf CLI + watchexec', which also works with the deployed editor from finding 2.

result.verdict_reason: The architecture (keep .wick format, new Rust compiler on the swf crate, Ruffle as player, hello-square first) is right-sized for a solo hobby and Phase 0 is genuinely well-designed. But the sequencing puts the nostalgic payoff behind the two historically lethal workstreams — the CRA fork revival and a two-renderer differential test harness — when the live deployed editor at wickeditor.com/editor/ makes the fork unnecessary for v1 and golden PNGs make the differential harness unnecessary, period. With Phase 2 demoted to optional, Phase 1 milestone-sliced, and the oracle downsized, the project delivers its personal payoff within weeks and can safely die any time after.
